item.title: PHP Date Comparison Techniques: Expired vs. Current Time
item.description:
“PHP Date Comparison Techniques: Expired vs. Current Time”

When dealing with data retrieved from a database, such as expiration dates for tokens, subscriptions, or items, accurately determining if the current time has passed the stored expiration date is a frequent programming requirement in PHP. How can we reliably perform this check using different available tools and data formats?

Utilizing Standard PHP Date Functions with Timestamps

For dates stored in a way that allows conversion to a UNIX timestamp (assuming dates are post-1970), the strtotime() function offers a straightforward path for comparison.

item.title: Java Date Comparison: Efficient Techniques for Checks
item.description:
“Java Date Comparison: Efficient Techniques for Checks”

When working with dates in Java, accurately comparing them is a fundamental requirement for many applications, from scheduling and event management to data validation. Several approaches exist, each with its strengths and nuances. This post delves into various methods for comparing java.util.Date objects and modern alternatives.

Solution 1: Using Date.before(), Date.after(), and Date.equals()

The java.util.Date class provides straightforward methods for comparison. before(), after(), and equals() allow you to determine the chronological relationship between two dates.
